name: Dual-horizon momentum persistence (15m)
rationale: Requiring BOTH a fast and a slower 15m return to be positive demands that momentum agrees across two horizons, screening out one-bar noise spikes that a single-lookback filter would chase. The alignment marks a genuinely persistent drift the trend-follower crowd is still feeding. The other side is the short-horizon fader repeatedly wrong-footed by continuation. Edge persists because multi-scale agreement is a stronger prior on drift than any single window. Distinct from single-return trend specs by construction. Disconfirmer: exits when the fast return flips negative (the shorter horizon rolled over) before the stop.
catalyst: momentum aligned across two return horizons
